headline.general: Principal Engineer · Production LLM platforms in regulated lending · Evaluations, provider failover, cost tracing · TypeScript, Node.js, AWS

summary.general: I build production LLM platforms for regulated mortgage lending. I spent 4.5 years as Staff Engineer at House Numbers, one of its first two non-founding engineers, as the team grew from three to seven. I built its LLM evaluation, provider-failover and deterministic-validation layers. When Dark Matter Technologies acquired the House Numbers platform and team, I joined as Principal Engineer.

general: Built and owned the communications service, keeping LLM classification separate from deterministic routing. It let operations retire manual-triage shifts and handled 57,000+ communications in a seven-month window.
Moved LLM infrastructure for four services off a vendor platform into an in-house layer with versioned prompts, provider failover, per-call cost tracing and evaluations.

Led the document-extraction evaluation audit and wrote its methodology (ground truth from printed values, exact matching, a hash-locked answer key), giving the team a reproducible baseline for under $10 across three runs.
Moved document checks from LLM generation to deterministic, tested validation, so loan processors get reproducible results.
Rebuilt routing for the public borrower document-upload flow, resolving recurring failed-upload complaints.
Wrote the engineering guide to handling PII in agent systems, later used to shape the company's data-retention and deletion work.

First engineer assigned to, then main backend engineer of, a multi-tenant SaaS for real-time quality-control inspections (NestJS, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, AWS, GitLab CI); owned backend architecture and delivery end to end.

Recovered a frustrated client's account after the project manager resigned: became the team's spokesperson, paired quick wins with core-workflow repairs, rebuilt trust within a few sprints and led the client product conversations for about six months; the client went on to commission additional projects.
Onboarded and mentored new engineers with an approach later adopted at House Numbers as a rotating buddy program; 15+ people onboarded across the two companies.

Led the platform's legacy-SAP data migration: evaluated ETL tooling, built custom scripts where existing tools could not represent the source and target models, validated rounding compatibility early with platform users, and needed no post-migration reconciliation.
Full-stack engineer (Node.js, React, PostgreSQL) on a procurement platform rebuilt for a US fiduciary purchasing agent (FF&E/OS&E).

Owned the migration of historical quote data out of a legacy SAP system with zero data loss: custom ETL, traced a financial-total discrepancy to SAP/JavaScript rounding differences, and ran a frozen cutover with snapshot-backed reconciliation; users retired the legacy system after MVP launch.

experience.compactLine: Acting technical lead: serverless architecture (Lambda, CloudFormation, DynamoDB) for a dynamic-document platform; led a four-person team delivering it.
Via Kubesoft SAS: migrated a real-time telecom monolith to an AWS Kubernetes microservices cluster; migrated a mobile backend off Parse ahead of its shutdown deadline.
Web/hybrid-mobile products for Colombian and international clients; built the first backend of Mutual, a hackathon-winning parenting app. From Feb 2016 assigned full-time to Rokk3r (above).
Real-time game backend with micropayments (Node.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, PHP) and its infrastructure.

projects.summary: Public MCP server, RAG-backed interview agent (Neon pgvector, Gemini embeddings) and Next.js site over one typed career dataset; Vitest, Playwright e2e against real Vercel previews, and retrieval/agent evals as required CI gates.

education.line: Universidad Nacional Abierta y a Distancia (UNAD) — coursework toward B.S. Systems Engineering
